items.q: If getting rich from investing is simple, why won't most people do it?
items.a: "Investing's been solved. We're going to use **index funds**. That's it. The hard part is actually **doing that**." Psychology and life design beat stock-picking. People who know "just enough to hurt themselves" underperform those who keep it simple.

items.q: Does checking your portfolio more often help?
items.a: No — academic finding: **more portfolio checks → less risk taken → lower returns**. Felix's parable: lose the password. Control plan, goals, allocation, emergency fund, and tax — **not market timing**.

items.q: How should you set financial goals that aren't just "more money"?
items.a: Use **PERMA** (Positive emotion, Engagement, Relationships, Meaning, Accomplishment) plus categorical prompts for higher-quality goals. Run the Ferrari **hedonic treadmill** test before optimizing for status purchases.

items.q: What's the real cost of a $10 coffee in Felix's framing?
items.a: At ~7% over 40 years, **$10 today ≈ $150** in future compounding. "You better really enjoy the coffee." Balance spending joy against **future compounding** deliberately.

items.q: What's the #1 mistake before frugality even matters?
items.a: **Not earning enough** — human capital, rare complementary skills, and market/industry choice often dominate (e.g. biotech writer **5× pay**). Other big misses: wrong risks (stock picking/options/crypto), tax/estate planning, partner money personality, and under-insuring (term life + disability).

items.q: How do you decide rent vs buy without the mortgage-vs-rent trap?
items.a: **5% housing rule**: unrecoverable costs ≈ mortgage interest + equity opportunity cost + property tax (~0.5–1%) + maintenance (~2%+). Monthly break-even rent ≈ price × 5% ÷ 12 (**$300K → $1,250/mo**). Controlled studies show **no owner happiness advantage**; buy for risk aversion, long tenure, priced-out fear, or primary-residence tax treatment.

sections.title: Allocation controversy and products to skip

items.q: Why does Felix challenge the bond glide path?
items.a: Bootstrap sim across **39 countries since 1890** finds **100% global equities** (≈⅓ domestic, ⅔ international) often optimal vs target-date bonds. Bonds got crushed in high inflation. Cash under a mattress: **3% inflation halves** purchasing power in ~20 years.

items.q: Which "smart" products should most people avoid?
items.a: Skip **covered-call ETFs** (capped upside), **thematic ETFs** launched at peaks (AI/cannabis/EV), and high-fee private-access products. Fees compound silently. No crypto at PWL; don't reallocate a diversified portfolio just because of crises.

items.q: How do money personalities wreck relationships?
items.a: **Tightwad–spendthrift mismatch** (Carnegie Mellon/Michigan quiz): opposites marry → more money conflict. Prenups as "default government will" analogy. Women often outperform men investing via **less overtrading** (Fidelity/Warwick/UC Berkeley findings) — "Give your money to your wife."
